title: Vowels Game in a String
spaceBreakdown:
- Loop variable c: O(1)
- No containers, arrays, or recursion allocated
- not counted: input string s
approach: The key insight is that Alice wins if and only if the string contains at least one vowel. If there are zero vowels, Alice cannot make any move (every substring has 0 vowels, which is even) and loses immediately. If there is at least one vowel, Alice can always force a win: if the vowel count is odd, she removes the entire string on her first turn; if even, she removes a single vowel, leaving an odd count for Bob - and after Bob's forced move (which always leaves an odd count since he can never remove the whole odd-vowel string), Alice removes the entire remaining string and wins.
hints: What is the only scenario in which Alice cannot make her first move? In Example 2, the string "bbcd" contains no vowels.
Scan the string once to check if any vowel exists. For "leetcoder", the second character 'e' is a vowel, so Alice can always force a win.

**Even vowel count** - Alice wins despite even parity
`Input: s = "ae"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning `vowel_count % 2 == 1` → returns false

**All consonants** - Alice has no valid move
`Input: s = "xyz"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning `s.length() > 0` → returns true

**Single vowel** - minimum winning input
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: requiring `vowel_count >= 2` → returns false

followUps.q: What if Bob goes first instead of Alice?
followUps.a: Bob needs an even-vowel substring. If there are 0 vowels, Bob removes any consonant and wins immediately. If there is exactly 1 vowel and no consonants, Bob cannot move and loses. With ≥2 vowels or ≥1 consonant alongside a vowel, Bob can move, making the outcome depend on both vowel and consonant counts rather than just vowel existence. TC: O(n), SC: O(1).

followUps.q: What if the string length is up to 10^9 and arrives as a character stream?
followUps.a: The solution already processes characters one at a time and returns on the first vowel found. It is naturally streaming-compatible - no buffering or storage of the full string is needed. TC: O(n) worst case, SC: O(1).

followUps.q: What if Alice must remove a substring with exactly k vowels instead of an odd number?
followUps.a: Alice can make her first move if and only if some substring contains exactly k vowels. Use prefix sums of vowel counts with a hash map to check existence in O(n). If no such substring exists, Alice loses immediately. TC: O(n), SC: O(n).
